subject: Solstice renewal: term shift + capacity increment — coordination on MSA & order form
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Garcia <ana@solstice.com>, Procurement <procurement@solstice.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Solstice renewal: term shift + capacity increment — proposal and order form

Hi Ana / Solstice procurement team,

Thanks again for the discussion yesterday. Per our call, attached is an updated order form (Solstice_OrderForm_v3.docx) that reflects: a 36-month term option (instead of the current 12-month), a +40% capacity uplift for the first 12 months, and the proposed pricing tiers with proration for the partial first month.

High-level notes:
- Term: proposing a 36-month primary term with annual review windows.
- Capacity: Exhibit B lists the baseline + 40% uplift; we included both committed and burst buckets.
- SLAs: no change from the MSA, but we can add a 30-day SLA credit cap for the expanded capacity during first 90 days if needed.

Can you confirm the preferred effective date (we penciled in 2028-09-01) and whether your procurement team needs any special billing cadence or PO fields?

I’ve looped in Ben (renewals) to confirm commercials and Marissa (legal) for the MSA/order form coordination. If it helps, happy to schedule a 30-minute redline review next week.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Solstice_OrderForm_v3.docx (order form with pricing tables), ExhibitB_capacity_schedule.xlsx (capacity table by month)

From: Ana Garcia <ana@solstice.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solstice.com>, Legal <legal@solstice.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice renewal: term shift + capacity increment — proposal and order form

Ava,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple quick clarifying questions from procurement/legal:

1) Exhibit B: can you confirm whether the committed capacity is guaranteed for the full 36 months or if the uplift is only firm for the first 12 months? Our finance team needs clarity for capitalization.
2) MSA: our legal team would like the MSA to reflect the longer term and add a mutual termination clause tied to force majeure and a data residency paragraph — are you able to share a redline of the MSA showing the proposed term language?
3) Billing: we generally prefer monthly invoicing, with PO number on the invoice. Will the proration be calculated on a daily basis for the first month?

We should be able to turn around comments within 3 business days once we have the redline.

Best,
Ana
CFO (acting)
Solstice, Inc.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Solstice renewal: term shift + capacity increment — proposal and order form

Looping legal and AE lead.

Ava — thanks for sending. Quick operational plan from my side:
- Commercials: the +40% uplift for year 1 keeps the unit price at the mid-tier; for years 2/3 we can offer a 5% step-down annual commit discount if they lock 36 months. I will add a short pricing appendix to the order form to capture that.
- Billing: yes to monthly invoices; proration = daily basis. Will confirm in the invoice template.
- Next step: Marissa, can you produce a marked-up MSA that shows the 36-month term language and cites the termination & data residency language (we expect minor edits)? If you can get a redline by EOD Monday, we can send to Solstice for their review.

Priyom — please confirm the expected cutover/start date impact on capacity provisioning (we proposed 2028-09-01). If we need earlier provisioning windows, call it out.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Garcia <ana@solstice.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jul 2028 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice renewal: term shift + capacity increment — MSA redline attached

Hi team — attaching MSA_redline_v2.docx with tracked changes that reflect:
- Section 2 (Term): proposed language for 36-month initial term with annual renewal windows and a 90-day performance review clause.
- Termination: added mutual termination for material breach with a 60-day cure period; clarified force majeure carve-outs.
- Data residency: added a paragraph requiring data at rest for Solstice EU-region customers to be stored in specified regions (if applicable) and a KMS reference.

Summary of questions for Solstice:
- Do you require the uplift to be contractually guaranteed for 36 months or just the first 12 months with renewal options?
- Any specific insurance/indemnity thresholds we should be aware of?

Quoted from Ana’s note below for context:
> Exhibit B: can you confirm whether the committed capacity is guaranteed for the full 36 months or if the uplift is only firm for the first 12 months?

I recommend we share the MSA redline + a single consolidated order form (Ben to add the pricing appendix) so Solstice can do one pass. If they come back with narrow redlines, we can triage and aim to finalize via DocuSign within 5 business days.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redline_v2.docx (tracked changes)

From: Ana Garcia <ana@solstice.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solstice renewal: term shift + capacity increment — MSA redline attached

Marissa / team,

Appreciate the redline. Procurement/legal reviewed and we have the following items:

1) Capacity guarantee: Solstice needs the committed uplift guaranteed for 12 months firm, with an option to extend to 36 months at the same committed level. We cannot commit to amortizing the uplift for 36 months without internal board approval.
2) Data residency: we are fine with the KMS reference but request language that allows certain customer datasets to remain within our US tenancy (we are not EU-facing for this account today).
3) Billing/proration: confirm daily proration and add the PO number field to the invoice template.

If you can incorporate those changes and send a consolidated package (final order form + MSA redline in a single thread), procurement can turn this in ~48 hours. We will need DocuSign once commercial terms are finalized.

Also — timeline: target signature date is 2028-08-15 to hit provisioning windows. If that’s tight for you, let us know and we can adjust.

Thanks,
Ana
CFO (acting)
Solstice, Inc.
